prognathodon-cipactli:table:1.title: 2026 in reptile paleontology (table of new taxa)

prognathodon-cipactli:study:1.title: A new species of Prognathodon (Squamata: Mosasauridae) from the Early Maastrichtian of Nuevo León, Mexico (Neues Jahrbuch für Geologie und Paläontologie - Abhandlungen, 2026)

facts.statement: The species was described by Rivera‑Sylva and colleagues.
facts.quote: Authors: Rivera-Sylva et al.

facts.statement: Prognathodon cipactli lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: The type specimen was recovered from the Méndez Shale in Mexico.
facts.quote: Type locality: Méndez Shale

facts.statement: Prognathodon cipactli is a valid taxon.
facts.quote: Status: Valid

facts.statement: The species belongs to the subfamily Mosasaurinae, a group of mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Notes: A mosasaur belonging to the subfamily Mosasaurinae; a species of Prognathodon.

facts.statement: The genus Prognathodon is classified within the Mosasaurinae subfamily alongside Mosasaurus and Clidastes.
facts.quote: It is classified as part of the Mosasaurinae subfamily, alongside genera like Mosasaurus and Clidastes.

facts.statement: Fossils of Prognathodon have been found in deposits ranging from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian across the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa and North America.
facts.quote: Prognathodon has been recovered from deposits ranging in age from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian in the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa and North America.

facts.statement: Prognathodon species typically have robust, conical teeth with blunt, serrated edges and smooth enamel.
facts.quote: Robust and conical teeth with blunt, serrated carinae and smooth enamel are often seen as typical Prognathodon teeth

facts.statement: The type species P. solvayi differs by having labio‑lingually compressed and gently facetted marginal teeth.
facts.quote: the type species P. solvayi differs from this type of teeth and instead exhibits markedly labio-lingually compressed and gently facetted marginal teeth

facts.statement: P. solvayi possesses 12 teeth on the maxilla and 13 teeth on the dentary.
facts.quote: P. solvayi has 12 teeth on the maxilla and 13 on the dentary

facts.statement: The largest known tooth crowns of P. lutugini reach up to 5.5 cm in height and 2.5 cm in width at the base.
facts.quote: The largest known tooth crowns are up to 5.5 cm tall and 2.5 cm wide at the base

facts.statement: P. lutugini tooth roots are about 1.5 times larger than the crowns and are barrel‑shaped.
facts.quote: The roots of the teeth are quite large at about 1.5 times the size of the tooth crowns and are barrel-shaped

facts.statement: The presence of a crescent‑shaped tail fluke indicates convergent evolution of mosasaurs with ichthyosaurs, metriorhynchid thalattosuchians and whales.
facts.quote: evidence that mosasaurs were convergent with ichthyosaurs, metriorhynchid thalattosuchians and whales in the evolution of a crescent-shaped tail fluke

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetic analyses place the genus Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Modern phylogenetic analyses continually place Prognathodon within the Mosasaurinae subfamily

facts.statement: Early researchers, including Louis Dollo, originally grouped Prognathodon with Platecarpus in a "microrhynchous" group based on rostrum and quadrate features.
facts.quote: Prognathodon was placed alongside Platecarpus in a "microrhynchous" group.

facts.statement: The genus Prognathodon is widely considered to be paraphyletic due to incomplete specimens and uncertain early Campanian records.
facts.quote: A large number of species have been assigned to Prognathodon, though the genus is widely considered to be paraphyletic.

facts.statement: Prognathodon solvayi, the type species, is the smallest known species at about 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: P. solvayi is the type species of Prognathodon and also the smallest known species at barely 5 meters in length.

facts.statement: Prognathodon lutugini possesses 13 dentary teeth, a feature it shares only with P. solvayi among the genus.
facts.quote: P. lutugini also differs from all other species except for P. solvayi by having 13 teeth in its dentary

facts.statement: Prognathodon cipactli was formally described in 2026 by Rivera‑Sylva, Sánchez‑Uribe, Guzmán‑Gutierrez, Rodríguez, Rangel‑Morelos, and Longrich.
facts.quote: P. cipactli Rivera-Sylva, Sánchez-Uribe, Guzmán-Gutierrez, Rodríguez, Rangel-Morelos, & Longrich, 2026

facts.statement: Prognathodon cipactli belongs to the family Mosasauridae, subfamily Mosasaurinae, and tribe Globidensini.
facts.quote:
familia: Mosasauridae
subfamilia: Mosasaurinae
tribus: Globidensini

facts.statement: The genus Prognathodon lived during the Late Cretaceous (Cretácico Superior).
facts.quote: vivieron durante el Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Fossils of Prognathodon have been found in what is now North America, Europe, and Africa.
facts.quote: en lo que actualmente es Norteamérica, Europa, y África

facts.statement: Prognathodon had bony rings surrounding its eye sockets, a feature interpreted as an adaptation to deep‑water habitats.
facts.quote: Poseía anillos óseos rodeando sus órbitas oculares, lo que indica que vivía en aguas profundas.

facts.statement: The skull of Prognathodon was large, relatively short, and had a rounded snout.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por un cráneo grande y relativamente corto. El cráneo era acinético, con una punta del hocico redondeada.

facts.statement: Prognathodon possessed large, conical teeth, with especially oversized teeth on the pterygoid bones.
facts.quote: Los dientes son grandes, cónicos, y los ubicados en el pterigoides eran muy grandes.

facts.statement: In some Prognathodon species the teeth projected forward, a condition comparable to Triassic placodonts and suggesting a diet that could include shellfish, large fish and marine turtles.
facts.quote: En algunas especies los dientes se extendían hacia adelante, como algunos de los placodontes que vivieron durante el Triásico, por lo que pueden haber tenido un estilo de vida parecido, alimentándose de mariscos, peces grandes y tortugas marinas, aunque en general serían depredadores generalistas.

facts.statement: The genus name Prognathodon means “tooth protruding from the jaw” in Greek, referring to its prominent teeth.
facts.quote: Estos dientes que sobresalían de la mandíbula son la razón del nombre de Prognathodon (en griego, "diente sobresaliendo de la mandíbula").
